hook.text: Tony Buzan popularized mind maps in the 1970s. A central idea radiates outward into branches of related concepts.

buildup.text: Place the main topic in the center. Draw branches for subtopics. Add smaller branches for details.

discovery.text: Mind maps mirror how the brain naturally associates ideas: radiantly, not linearly.

twist.text: Mind maps are poor for sequential information like step-by-step processes. They excel at relationships, not timelines.

climax.text: Use mind maps for brainstorming, topic overviews, and planning. Switch to linear notes for detailed sequential content.

punchline.text: Center the idea. Branch out. See the connections appear.

quiz.question: When are mind maps most effective?
options: For brainstorming, overviews, and seeing relationships between ideas
For taking notes during fast-paced lectures
